Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

path = Path('sklearn/model_selection/_search.py')

            if y is not None:

            self.best_estimator_ = clone(base_estimator).set_params(
                **self.best_params_)
            refit_start_time = time.time()
            if y is not None:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, y, **fit_params)
            else:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, **fit_params)
            refit_end_time = time.time()
            self.refit_time_ = refit_end_time - refit_start_time

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

import time

import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)


X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

search = GridSearchCV(
    SlowRegressor(delay=0.05),
    {"value": [1.0, 2.0]},
    cv=KFold(n_splits=2, shuffle=True, random_state=0),
)
search.fit(X, y)
print("refit_time_: {!r}".format(search.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float)
assert search.refit_time_ >= 0.05

no_refit.fit(X, y)
print("has refit_time_ with refit=False: {}".format(hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")))

parallel.fit(X, y)
print("parallel refit_time_: {!r}".format(parallel.refit_time_))

assert parallel.refit_time_ >= 0

unsupervised = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0]}, cv=2)

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

import time

import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)


X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

import time

import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)


X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

search = GridSearchCV(
    SlowRegressor(delay=0.05),
    {"value": [1.0, 2.0]},
    cv=KFold(n_splits=2, shuffle=True, random_state=0),
)
search.fit(X, y)
print("refit_time_: {!r}".format(search.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float)
assert search.refit_time_ >= 0.05

no_refit = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(), {"value": [1.0]}, refit=False, cv=2)
no_refit.fit(X, y)
print("has refit_time_ with refit=False: {}".format(hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")))

parallel = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0, 2.0]}, cv=2, n_jobs=2)
parallel.fit(X, y)
print("parallel refit_time_: {!r}".format(parallel.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(parallel.refit_time_, float)
assert parallel.refit_time_ >= 0

unsupervised = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0]}, cv=2)
unsupervised.fit(X)
assert unsupervised.refit_time_ >= 0
print("all checks passed")

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

I’ll implement the change now: import `time`, measure only the best estimator’s refit call, expose the duration as `refit_time_` when refitting occurs, and document the new attribute on both search classes.

from pathlib import Path

path = Path('sklearn/model_selection/_search.py')
text = path.read_text()

old_import = "import operator\nimport warnings\n"
new_import = "import operator\nimport time\nimport warnings\n"
assert text.count(old_import) == 1
text = text.replace(old_import, new_import, 1)

old_refit = """        if self.refit:
            self.best_estimator_ = clone(base_estimator).set_params(
                **self.best_params_)
            if y is not None:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, y, **fit_params)
            else:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, **fit_params)
"""
new_refit = """        if self.refit:
            self.best_estimator_ = clone(base_estimator).set_params(
                **self.best_params_)
            refit_start_time = time.time()
            if y is not None:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, y, **fit_params)
            else:
                self.best_estimator_.fit(X, **fit_params)
            refit_end_time = time.time()
            self.refit_time_ = refit_end_time - refit_start_time
"""
assert text.count(old_refit) == 1
text = text.replace(old_refit, new_refit, 1)

old_doc = """    n_splits_ : int
        The number of cross-validation splits (folds/iterations).

"""
new_doc = """    n_splits_ : int
        The number of cross-validation splits (folds/iterations).

    refit_time_ : float
        Time in seconds used for refitting the best model on the whole dataset.

        This is present only if ``refit`` is not False.

"""
assert text.count(old_doc) == 2
text = text.replace(old_doc, new_doc)

path.write_text(text)

import time

import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)


X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

search = GridSearchCV(
    SlowRegressor(delay=0.05),
    {"value": [1.0, 2.0]},
    cv=KFold(n_splits=2, shuffle=True, random_state=0),
)
search.fit(X, y)
print("refit_time_: {!r}".format(search.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float)
assert search.refit_time_ >= 0.05

no_refit = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(), {"value": [1.0]}, refit=False, cv=2)
no_refit.fit(X, y)
print("has refit_time_ with refit=False: {}".format(hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")))
assert not hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")

parallel = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0, 2.0]}, cv=2, n_jobs=2)
parallel.fit(X, y)
print("parallel refit_time_: {!r}".format(parallel.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(parallel.refit_time_, float)
assert parallel.refit_time_ >= 0

unsupervised = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0]}, cv=2)
unsupervised.fit(X)
assert unsupervised.refit_time_ >= 0
print("all checks passed")

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

import time

import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold


class SlowRegressor(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin):
    def __init__(self, delay=0.0, value=1.0):
        self.delay = delay
        self.value = value

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        time.sleep(self.delay)
        self.mean_ = float(np.mean(y)) if y is not None else 0.0
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        return np.full(X.shape[0], self.mean_)


X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

search = GridSearchCV(
    SlowRegressor(delay=0.05),
    {"value": [1.0, 2.0]},
    cv=KFold(n_splits=2, shuffle=True, random_state=0),
)
search.fit(X, y)
print("refit_time_: {!r}".format(search.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float)
assert search.refit_time_ >= 0.05

no_refit = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(), {"value": [1.0]}, refit=False, cv=2)
no_refit.fit(X, y)
print("has refit_time_ with refit=False: {}".format(hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")))
assert not hasattr(no_refit, "refit_time_")

parallel = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0, 2.0]}, cv=2, n_jobs=2)
parallel.fit(X, y)
print("parallel refit_time_: {!r}".format(parallel.refit_time_))
assert isinstance(parallel.refit_time_, float)
assert parallel.refit_time_ >= 0

unsupervised = GridSearchCV(SlowRegressor(delay=0.01), {"value": [1.0]}, cv=2)
unsupervised.fit(X)
assert unsupervised.refit_time_ >= 0
print("all checks passed")
